title: Consumption horizon: sliding-window anchoring and safe resets for reserved pools
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Problem: Reserved pools and rolling-window quotas are drifting in production when tenants cross timezone boundaries, when capacity failovers occur, or when historical backfills happen. Existing epoch-based reset logic causes billing anomalies for multi-day sliding windows and creates hard-to-reproduce overage events for dedicated customers. Goal: Introduce a deterministic 'consumption horizon' anchoring mechanism that defines a moving window origin per-tenant and per-pool, supporting safe soft-resets, idempotent backfills, and reconciliations without requiring global epoch alignment. Scope: - Define consumption_horizon metadata and lease tokens for reserved pools. - Implement window-anchor arithmetic for N-day sliding windows and monthly-aligned windows with tenant-local timezone awareness. - Safe reset semantics: soft-decrement, grace buffers, and auto-repair via ledger snapshots. - Reconciliation tools: deterministic backfill plan, repair ops, and audit trail entries for billing. Acceptance criteria: 1) No customer-visible billing deltas >0.5% after pilot on 5 tenants for 30 days. 2) Deterministic ledger replay that produces bit-for-bit identical quotas for identical inputs. 3) Migration path that allows rolling upgrade of collectors without downtime. Implementation notes: - Use per-tenant logical epoch anchored on consumption_horizon (ISO8601 timestamp) stored with lease fencing. - Reset operation offers modes: preview, dry-run, soft-reset (adjust only counters), hard-reset (rewrite allocations and emit audit log). - Add reconciliation job that runs nightly to detect horizon drift >5 minutes and schedule corrective reanchors with exponential backoff. - Telemetry: add metrics quota.horizon.shift, quota.soft_reset.count, quota.reconcile.actions and a dashboard for reserved pools. Rollout plan: - Stage 1: unit/integration tests + canary on internal tenant. - Stage 2: pilot with 5 reserved customers (low traffic) for two billing cycles. - Stage 3: open rollout with 2-week observation window and auto-rollback on anomalies. Migration: collector change is backward compatible; new lease token validity window is additive. Documentation: Confluence design doc (link below) with operator runbook and rollback steps.
